narrative.overview:
cognilogs looks like an operations notebook that has been edited into a public argument: cool paper, black ink, orange signal, and real interface fragments. The system borrows the scale and confidence of editorial poster design, but every large gesture resolves into a support artifact. A ticket, a run, an evidence card, and an SLA watch are the vocabulary. The visitor should be able to see the loop close, not just read a promise that it does.

The visual world is paper-light and deliberately flat. White sheets sit on a cool paper ground, separated by hairlines and tonal tints rather than shadows. Orange appears as a signal: the wordmark, an active dot, a focus ring, the waitlist surface. Blue, green, and pink carry meaning about work types and confidence states. A near-black console is the one dark room, used where the product performs machine work. Nothing floats decoratively.

Local deployment is part of the visual argument. A dashed network boundary contains the app, ticket data, and the SLA worker; external services are named separately. Compliance copy describes control and review scope, never a certification that has not been issued.

The tone is confident, operational, and honest. Diagrams are built from HTML interface fragments and custom inline SVG line work. The page never pretends to show a production screenshot, a customer logo, or a benchmark. The reference grammar is MausBot's editorial structure, never its mascots, assets, or copy.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground and white sheets, with hairline separators.
Oversized Inter display type against dense, readable interface fragments.
Orange as a scarce signal color, not a decorative wash.
Colored nodes and dotted paths that explain support work.
One near-black console for machine output and evidence.
Rounded sheets, pills, and ticket cards with no ornamental shadows.
A deployment boundary that shows what stays inside the customer's network.
Motion that demonstrates state, then gets out of the way.

rules.name: The Signal Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange is a signal, not a background. Outside the waitlist hero and small tinted sheets, it should appear in dots, words, focus rings, and single actions. If orange covers a large surface, that surface must be the commitment itself.

rules.name: The One Meaning Per Color Rule
rules.body: Blue, green, and pink always describe work type or confidence state. Never use them as decorative variety in the same diagram.

rules.name: The No Decorative Gradient Rule
rules.body: Gradients and glows are not part of the visual world. The marquee fade is a functional edge mask, not decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Font Rule
rules.body: Inter runs the interface and the argument. JetBrains Mono is a costume for machine output, not a second brand voice.

rules.name: The 13px Floor Rule
rules.body: Shared chrome, legal fine print, and body-adjacent labels do not go below 13px. Smaller type is allowed only inside data-dense interface fragments and SVG microtype, where it is part of the artifact.

rules.name: The 600px Prose Rule
rules.body: Docs paragraphs and legal articles both max out at 600px. Do not use ch units for these measures with Inter.

rules.name: The 320px Rule
rules.body: Every route must survive 320px with no horizontal scroll. Decorative wordmark echoes and diagram paths are clipped by their own containers, not by the page root.

rules.name: The Sidebar Rest Rule
rules.body: Desktop docs and legal sidebars rest at 112px below the viewport top and stick there. Their columns must remain tall enough to scroll through the full article.

rules.name: The Form First Rule
rules.body: On mobile, the waitlist form comes before the supporting benefits. The primary action should be reachable in the first viewport whenever the copy allows it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs separation, use a hairline, a tint, or a dark panel. Do not reach for a shadow.

rules.name: The One Dark Room Rule
rules.body: The near-black console is the only large dark surface. Use it for machine work and evidence, not for arbitrary emphasis.

rules.name: The Sheet, Not Card Rule
rules.body: A container should feel like a sheet of paper laid on the page, not a floating app card. Keep the radius generous, the border quiet, and the shadow absent.

rules.name: The Diagram Is an Interface Rule
rules.body: Every diagram must contain a real support object: a ticket, a source, a confidence score, a run log, a child ticket, or an SLA clock. If it could be replaced by a generic icon, it is not a cognilogs diagram.

dos: Do keep the paper ground, white sheets, and orange signal in that order of area.
Do use giant Inter headlines and let interface fragments carry the detail.
Do show the loop with tickets, sources, confidence scores, child tickets, and SLA watches.
Do label official brand marks in the trust rail and keep ticketing systems generic; there is no First/Planned connector ladder.
Do keep shared chrome and legal fine print at 13px or above.

Do use Next Link for internal links and serve local builds from the domain root. The GitHub Pages project build sets GITHUB_PAGES=true and uses /landing as its base path. Do not hard-code a base path into local development.
Do show the deployment boundary and name external dependencies before a pilot.
Do keep the confidence slider at a fixed 0.92 evidence score; only the threshold moves.
Do provide a static, wrapping trust-strip fallback under reduced motion and hide the pause control there.
Do keep docs prose and legal articles at 600px.
Do use CSS chevrons and colored dots instead of decorative arrow SVGs or icon medallions.
Do preserve the Google Sheets waitlist integration and its success/error states.
donts: Don't use stock photography, raster screenshots, mascots, or AI-generated illustrations.
Don't invent customer logos, testimonials, benchmarks, pricing, production claims, or certifications.
Don't imply that local deployment guarantees compliance. Certification work is in progress; keep the language positive and limited.
Don't describe any connector as live unless the deployment confirms it.
Don't use decorative gradients, glows, blurred halos, or ornamental shadows.
Don't put uppercase kickers above every section; the editorial hierarchy should come from scale and position.
Don't add stage numbers, icon medallions, or decorative arrows to the architecture map.
Don't reintroduce page-root overflow-hidden; use overflow-x: clip and clip decorations locally.
Don't use 68ch for docs prose; Inter makes it roughly 720px and produces 90-character lines.
Don't use the MausBot palette, mascots, assets, or verbatim copy. The structural grammar is the reference, not the identity.
Don't replace the waitlist webhook with a new backend without an explicit request.
